summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would authorise spending from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for the ordinary annual services of the government.

It would provide about 5/12ths of the estimated 2025-26 annual appropriations for those services, with a larger share for entities like the National Emergency Management Agency that have high early-year spending.
The remaining 7/12ths plus 2025-26 Budget measures would be covered by a separate bill, the Appropriation Bill (No. 1) 2025-2026.
changes: Proposes appropriations from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for ordinary annual services.
Sets the appropriation amount at broadly 5/12ths of estimated 2025-26 annual appropriations.
Allows a greater proportion for certain entities with high early-year expenditure or service delivery needs.
summary.affected: The government and its entities, particularly those with high early-year spending such as the National Emergency Management Agency.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Moved procedural arrangements to sequence debate and votes on Supply Bills, the Transport Security Amendment Bill 2024, the Parliamentary Business Resources Legislation Amendment Bill 2025 and the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment Bill 2025. Said the motion was needed because Senate estimates would prevent later consideration.

speeches.speaker: Lisa Chesters
speeches.brief: Reported that debate time had expired under an earlier resolution and put the questions required to complete consideration of the listed bills; the question was agreed to and the bill was read a second time.

speeches.speaker: Jenny McAllister
speeches.brief: Tabled proposed and certain proposed expenditure for the year ending on 30 June 2026, including expenditure for parliamentary departments and the Supply Bill (No. 1) 2025-2026 and Supply Bill (No. 2) 2025-2026, then moved for referral to legislation committees; the motion was agreed to.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Chisholm
speeches.brief: Moved and amended a Senate business motion setting meeting hours, ordering consideration and expedited voting on listed bills, providing for valedictory statements and budget responses, allowing divisions after 6.30 pm, and adding further bills before the motion was agreed to.
